A1.justification: Both complete 28-page PDFs describe the same PFPO study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PFPO experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation in Tables 1–3, alongside synthetic-test-case analyses and additional experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original PFPO benchmark results, iterative-training experiments, synthetic-test-case analyses, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The frontier-LLM and self-consistency feedback procedures, outcome/process preference construction, DPO objective, and iterative training are unchanged. Figure 2 corrects illustrative correctness markers without changing the method specified in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MathScale/NuminaMath and APPs/Magicoder/xCodeEval training sources and the same mathematical-reasoning and coding benchmarks. The MATH-Challenging subset in Appendix A.4 is also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including the SFT, DPO/pDPO, frontier-model, and open-model comparisons in Tables 1–3 and 9–12.

E3.justification: Training splits, filtering, model configurations, metrics, and evaluation procedures match. Both retain zero-shot greedy evaluation by default and the LiveCodeBench protocol of 10 samples at temperature 0.2 with the same date window. Appendix settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The synthetic-test-count ablation, test-case quality analysis, self-consistency analyses, and inference-scaling experiments in Sections 4.3–4.6 are retained. Appendix A preserves the DPO/pDPO comparison, challenging-subset evaluation, and training-order experiments.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither revision introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the existing sampling and estimation descriptions are retained.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in the main and appendix result tables and plotted results in Figures 3–5 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Mathstral's 68.6 MATH result, and Table 3 retains the 24.6 LiveCodeBench result. Figure 2's edited example is not an experimental result.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including reward definitions, majority voting, preference-pair conditions, and optimization objectives, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about frontier-LLM and generalized self-consistency feedback, scalable iterative preference optimization, and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The explanations involving synthetic-test coverage, distribution mismatch, feedback quality, and iterative-training saturation are unchanged. Appendix A.3 retains the same qualifications about access to unseen high-quality problems and limits on constructing valid preference pairs.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote stating that code is released and providing the Microsoft unilm/PFPO repository location. This adds code-access information absent from v1. Table 7 hyperparameters, Appendix C prompts, and Appendix D implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to self-improvement, mathematical reasoning, and code-generation research. The publication-status header does not revise that positioning.

P1.justification: The header changes from 'Work in Progress' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025,' and Table 1 corrects '/w' to 'w/'. Apart from the added code footnote, substantive prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is slightly resized and switches the correctness markers: answer 16 becomes incorrect and answer 7 correct, matching the pseudo-label. Its displayed preference ordering remains unchanged. Other figures and table structures are retained, with minor pagination and layout shifts.

improvement.justification: The new code-access footnote improves reproducibility documentation, and Figure 2 partially corrects a misleading illustration. These are limited benefits: the figure still displays the opposite preference ordering, while the scientific methods, evidence, and appendices remain unchanged.
